note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ERI 4; A06b ERI 4; L05 ERI 8(1)(a), 8(1)(c)): ordinary naturalisation after 20 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.said: Person is not of 'Eritrean origin' and has been legally resident in Eritrea for at least 10 years before 1974 or at least 20 years while making visits abroad. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person voluntarily acquires another citizenship or signs an oath of allegiance to another country after publication of the 1992 Proclamation (=nationality law). ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Eritrea to a father or mother of 'Eritrean origin' (tracing ancestry to a person resident in Eritrea in 1933). Person is born of an Eritrean father or mother. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a father or mother of 'Eritrean origin' (tracing ancestry to a person resident in Eritrea in 1933). Person is born of an Eritrean father or mother. ... No provision ... No provision
